An object will balance at its centre of gravity because, at this point,
the line of action of the object's weight passes through the pivot.
As a result, the weight does not create any moment (or torque)
around the pivot since there is no perpendicular distance from the
pivot to the line of action of the weight.
This means there is no net moment acting on the object, allowing it
to remain in equilibrium and balanced.
